title: The War Started by a Hungry Pig

chapters.title: The Shot Heard Round the Trough

scenes.narration: In 1859, the United States and the British Empire nearly plunged the globe into total war over one *dead potato-eating pig*.
scenes.image: Lyman Cutlar staring down in wide-eyed shock with a smoking musket at a large black boar sprawled in a potato patch.

scenes.narration: That unfortunate hog belonged to the British Hudson's Bay Company, and the potato patch belonged to Lyman Cutlar, an *American squatter*.
scenes.image: Lyman Cutlar pointing defensively at his ruined vegetable garden while Charles Griffin rushes toward him waving a leather ledger in fury.

scenes.narration: Cutlar woke up one morning, discovered the massive black Berkshire boar ravaging his prized tubers, and completely *lost his temper*.
scenes.image: Lyman Cutlar looking out his cabin window with steam blowing out of his ears as a fat pig happily crunches raw potatoes.

scenes.narration: Instead of chasing it off, Cutlar grabbed his musket, took deliberate aim, and turned the trespasser into *immediate bacon*.
scenes.image: Lyman Cutlar aiming his long musket through the window frame, cartoon muzzle smoke bursting outward.

scenes.narration: Stricken with remorse, Cutlar marched over to the pig's keeper, Charles Griffin, and sheepishly offered ten dollars in *cash restitution*.
scenes.image: Lyman Cutlar sheepishly holding out a tiny crumpled wad of dollar bills toward Charles Griffin.

scenes.narration: Griffin scoffed with immense indignity and demanded a hundred dollars, prompting Cutlar to shout that the pig was *eating his potatoes*.
scenes.image: Charles Griffin turning his nose to the sky with arms crossed while Lyman Cutlar gestures wildly toward the dirt.

scenes.narration: Griffin famously snapped back that it was up to Cutlar to keep his precious potatoes out of *the pig*.
scenes.image: Charles Griffin leaning nose-to-nose with Lyman Cutlar, tapping him condescendingly on the chest.

chapters.title: A Bad Map and Worse Borders

scenes.narration: How on earth did an argument over backyard root vegetables almost spark a catastrophic *international bloodbath*?
scenes.image: A spinning cartoon globe with a spotlight focusing on a tiny dot of land between Vancouver Island and Washington Territory.

scenes.narration: Thirteen years earlier, Britain and the United States signed the Oregon Treaty to partition the Pacific Northwest along the *forty-ninth parallel*.
scenes.image: Two stiff diplomats in nineteenth-century formal coats using a giant wooden ruler to draw a red line across a map.

scenes.narration: The agreement dictated that the border would follow the parallel straight to the middle of the channel separating *Vancouver Island*.
scenes.image: The diplomats staring intently at a maritime chart of San Juan Island, looking completely baffled by the multiple waterways.

scenes.narration: There was just one glaring, unforgivable mistake in the treaty: the diplomats forgot to specify *which channel*.
scenes.image: Two giant cartoon hands from opposite sides of the map pointing at two different sea straits surrounding the island.

scenes.narration: The British argued the border ran through Rosario Strait to the east, awarding them beautiful San Juan Island for *sheep farming*.
scenes.image: Charles Griffin standing proudly on a lush hillside surrounded by dozens of round fluffy sheep.

scenes.narration: The Americans swore the line ran down Haro Strait to the west, meaning the entire island belonged to *Uncle Sam*.
scenes.image: Lyman Cutlar firmly planting a wooden American flag stake right into the middle of a sheep grazing meadow.

scenes.narration: With zero consensus, both nations quietly flooded the disputed paradise with settlers and hoped nobody did anything *catastrophically dumb*.
scenes.image: American settlers in flannel and British sheep herders in tweed eyeing each other suspiciously across a rickety fence.

scenes.narration: Did the British authorities gently fine the trigger-happy farmer, or did they immediately threaten him with *unforgiving prison irons*?
scenes.image: Charles Griffin standing next to a stern British constable holding a pair of heavy iron shackles toward Lyman Cutlar.

scenes.narration: British magistrates warned Cutlar he could be arrested and tried under royal law, which sent the island's Americans into *sheer panic*.
scenes.image: Lyman Cutlar running in terror toward a small wooden shack where several American frontiersmen look alarmed.

scenes.narration: Cutlar and his panicked neighbors fired off an urgent petition to General William Harney, the fiery commander of the *Department of Oregon*.
scenes.image: A frightened messenger thrusting a parchment paper into the hands of General William Harney.

scenes.narration: Harney was an abrasive expansionist who despised the British and was privately salivating for any excuse to start a *patriotic brawl*.
scenes.image: General William Harney grinning maliciously while menacingly sharpening his heavy saber on a whetstone.

scenes.narration: Without waiting for orders from Washington, Harney rushed sixty-six armed infantrymen to the island under Captain George Pickett, the future *Confederate general*.
scenes.image: Captain George Pickett posing theatrically on the bow of a wooden steamship with soldiers packed behind him.

scenes.narration: Pickett strutted ashore on San Juan Island, hoisted the Stars and Stripes, and declared the rock under *exclusive American control*.
scenes.image: Captain George Pickett proudly hammering a tall American flag into the grass while Charles Griffin glares from behind a barn.

scenes.narration: Pickett warned that any British attempt to disembark would be answered with gunsmoke, promising to make a *bloody stand*.
scenes.image: Captain George Pickett standing behind a low earthen trench, dramatically brandishing his sword at the open sea.

scenes.narration: What does a royal governor do when a foreign army illegally occupies territory he considers *His Majesty's soil*?
scenes.image: James Douglas, the royal governor of Vancouver Island, stomping his boots and shaking his fists in wild anger on a harbor dock.

scenes.narration: James Douglas, the governor of Vancouver Island, dispatched three massive Royal Navy warships to anchor directly in front of *Pickett's camp*.
scenes.image: Three massive British three-masted wooden warships dropping heavy anchors in the bay, bristling with black cannon ports.

scenes.narration: Pickett, staring down dozens of heavy naval cannons with sixty-six riflemen, chose not to retreat, but to *dig in deeper*.
scenes.image: Captain George Pickett frantically ordering small American soldiers with shovels to dig dirt trenches on top of a hill.

scenes.narration: Pickett boasted that his men would fight to the last breath, even as more towering British *warships arrived*.
scenes.image: Captain George Pickett peering through a brass telescope, sweating as more British masts appear over the ocean horizon.

scenes.narration: Within weeks, the British naval force exploded to five formidable warships carrying over two thousand sailors and seventy-two *heavy guns*.
scenes.image: A fleet of five grand British warships completely surrounding the island shoreline with massive cannons aimed inland.

scenes.narration: American reinforcements sneaked past the blockade under heavy coastal fog, boosting Pickett's garrison to nearly five hundred men and *fourteen cannons*.
scenes.image: Rowboats full of blue-coated American soldiers silently hauling cannons onto the beach through thick white cartoon mist.

scenes.narration: For agonizing weeks, hundreds of men stood at hair-trigger battle stations, waiting for one nervous recruit to *pull a trigger*.
scenes.image: A British royal marine with a sweating hand hovering inches above a smoking cannon fuse, eyes wide with tension.

scenes.narration: With enough gunpowder on the island to vaporize the coastline, why did nobody actually fire the *catastrophic opening salvo*?
scenes.image: Admiral Robert Baynes standing on the deck of his flagship with arms crossed, calmly sipping tea amid armed marines.

scenes.narration: Governor Douglas continuously pushed the British fleet commander, Admiral Robert Baynes, to land the marines and *blast the Americans*.
scenes.image: Governor Douglas yelling directly into the ear of Admiral Robert Baynes, pointing his cane violently toward the island.

scenes.narration: But Admiral Baynes possessed the one trait missing from the crisis: common sense, refusing to start a world war over *a pig*.
scenes.image: Admiral Robert Baynes pushing Douglas away with one finger while casually inspecting his biscuit.

scenes.narration: When the news finally reached Washington D.C., President James Buchanan was horrified to discover a general was *risking war with Britain*.
scenes.image: President James Buchanan dropping his fountain pen and clutching his head in horror at a desk piled with urgent dispatches.

scenes.narration: Buchanan immediately dispatched General Winfield Scott, the seventy-three-year-old hero of the Mexican War, to travel cross-continent and *quell the madness*.
scenes.image: General Winfield Scott, immense and elderly in a gold-braided uniform, boarding a steamship while leaning heavily on a cane.

scenes.narration: Scott negotiated smoothly with British officials, establishing a peaceful joint military occupation and reducing both garrisons to just *one hundred men*.
scenes.image: General Winfield Scott shaking hands with a polite British officer over a small wooden table pitched in the forest.

scenes.narration: So how did this bizarre standoff finally resolve itself without a single drop of human *blood being spilled*?
scenes.image: An American soldier and a British marine sitting on wooden crates playing cards together peacefully between their camps.

scenes.narration: For twelve cozy years, British and American garrisons lived on opposite ends of the island, regularly attending each other's *holiday parties*.
scenes.image: American and British soldiers in full uniforms clinking cider mugs and sharing roasted turkey around an outdoor table.

scenes.narration: By 1871, both nations finally referred the boundary dispute to an independent arbitrator, Germany's Kaiser *Wilhelm the First*.
scenes.image: Kaiser Wilhelm I wearing a spiked Pickelhaube helmet, squinting through a large magnifying glass at a map of North America.

scenes.narration: The Kaiser's international commission evaluated the maps and officially decreed that Haro Strait was the proper border, awarding San Juan to *America*.
scenes.image: Kaiser Wilhelm I firmly pressing a heavy wax stamp right over San Juan Island on the treaty desk.

scenes.narration: In 1872, the British garrison politely dismantled their camp, shook hands with the Americans, and sailed away for *Vancouver Island*.
scenes.image: British soldiers boarding their rowboats while happily waving their caps to the American soldiers standing on the beach.

scenes.narration: The entire Pig War resulted in zero human casualties and one dead hog, leaving us to wonder what other *insane conflicts* history hid.
scenes.image: A small stone grave marker in a green potato field with a cartoon pig wearing angel wings floating happily above it.

description: In 1859, the United States and Great Britain came inches away from a devastating global war. The cause? An American squatter shot an English pig in a potato patch.
thumbnail_image: A giant furious black pig chewing on a potato while five enormous British warships and an army of American soldiers face off in the background.
